messages.author: 22d6bf0e16759db6
messages.subject: Stan + pymc3 users out there?
parts:
Hi everyone,

Is there anyone on this list that has experimented with pymc3, and can attest as to whether it's ready for prime time?

https://github.com/pymc-devs/pymc3

Apparently pymc3 implements NUTS via Theano's automatic differentiation engine. Using Theano means that theoretically you could even sample from models using the GPU; I'm curious if this actually works/provides a decent speed-up for big models.

(I ran into this by thinking, hey, if there were an autodiff engine built on Python, that would be a nice way to implement NUTS. And Googled it. And discovered, hey, cool, there is one, and somebody has implemented NUTS that way.)

Even if it's not ready, I can see pymc3's approach as having some big advantages over Stan's over the long term, and I imagine wouldn't be too hard to write a Stan-to-pymc3 cross-compiler so you could reuse existing models/continue to use the Stan language.

Ed

messages.author: 49e107cb0f8a3d27
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Stan + pymc3 users out there?
parts:
Hi, I don’t know of people specifically who take advantage of pymc3’s GPU support for NUTS but certainly it is being done. There are implementations of HMC in TensorFlow (not NUTS) that share the same benefits; for research purposes I’m also playing with HMC code written in these computational graph frameworks, as I needed to try MCMC as a baseline method for some big data sets and it could not done fast enough in Stan.

When I last checked, pymc3 is slower on CPUs than Stan, and it does an adaptation phase that isn’t as optimized as the one in Stan. My high-level understanding of the library is that it’s slower in terms of getting behind new ideas and their implementation (e.g., they’re still working on ADVI), but they do have added advantages due to the backend using computational graphs for symbolic diffs and enabling GPUs.

A cross-compiler would be cool but also difficult. If it underlies Stan’s call to functions such as log prob and grad log prob, then these would need to enable GPU support as well (after all that’s where the bottleneck in computation goes). So if someone develops one, then we should use it in native Stan too!

Dustin

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Stan + pymc3 users out there?
parts:
Is there a description somewhere of what exactly
Theano does? I can't figure it out from looking at
their doc and couldn't find something like a comprehensive
manual anywhere. In particular, I'm curious about

* what functions can be differentiated,
* what algorithm it uses to generate derivatives,
* what algorithm it uses to generate Hessians,
* how results of shared operations are reused,
* how it would calculate compound operations like
directional derivatives (I think they call those R-ops),
* how it could utilize GPU,

and of course,

* how fast is it for realistic problems, and
* are there problems it's particularly good or bad at?

- Bob
